content: Using this methodology, we can see how much exposure to new data it takes for a given model to master a new task, and whether there are phenomena that stress particular models (e.g., lead to catastrophic forgetting of the original task). Given the restrictions on the number of fine-tuning examples, our assumption is that when models are able to maintain good performance on their original task during inoculation, the quickness with which they are able to learn the inoculated task provides evidence of prior competence, which is precisely what we aim to probe. To measure past performance, we define a model's inoculation cost as the difference in the performance of this model on its original task before and after inoculation.
